newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Norilsk managers see possible strike but hopeful.
newsitem.headline: Norilsk managers see possible strike but hopeful.

text.p: Russia's Norilsk Nickel group is hopeful of reaching an agreement with trade unions at its flagship plant, where workers plan strikes on March 27 and April 2, a company spokesman said on Thursday.
But Anatoly Komrakov, who speaks for Norilsk's management, also said that he still had not ruled out the possibility of full-scale action by workers over salary and holiday arrears.

"The main thing is that the (strike) coordinating committee has not taken a final decision on the April 2 strike. It's preliminary," he said. "The committee has stressed that the process of talks (with management) will continue.
"But there is a proposal for a fullscale strike," he said.
A strike committee at the plant said earlier this week it would hold a one-hour warning strike on March 27 followed by fuller action on April 2.
RAO Norilsky Nickel 0#NKEL.RUO owes workers around 900 billion roubles ($160 million) and a further 1.2 trillion roubles ($211 million) to various budgets.
It plans to pay off arrears by the end of the year, but workers have demanded speedier payments.
